title: Kidney beans, from canned, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Canned kidney beans with added fat are a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole beans that are blanched, cooked, and then sealed in their own liquid with the addition of vegetable oil. The beans have a rich, slightly sweet flavor and a firm texture, while the added fat increases caloric density and makes them more satisfying.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kidney beans are named for their characteristic kidney‑shaped seeds.
Canning preserves the beans for several years while retaining most nutrients.
Added oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Beans are a staple protein source in vegetarian and vegan diets.
In the United States canned kidney beans are commonly used in chili, salads, and soups.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for blood formation and preventing anemia.

items.title: Source of plant antioxidants
items.content: Kidney beans contain polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added oil helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E, and K more efficiently.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Toxin in raw beans
items.content: Raw or undercooked kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxin that is destroyed during proper cooking and canning.

items.title: High caloric density
items.content: The added fat raises the calorie count, which may be a concern for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The beans are ready straight from the can: add them to salads, chili, soups, stews, or use as a filling for tacos. They can also be quickly warmed in a skillet with vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.
